name: Multi-level, multi-resolution page table hierarchy
definition: A data structure that decouples the down-sampling ratio of volume data from the hierarchy level count for address translation scalability. It allows choosing a down-sampling ratio based on quality requirements and a page table size reduction ratio based on scalability requirements, solving the inherent coupling in single tree structures where N determines both.
summary: This method decouples spatial subdivision from resolution levels using separate page table hierarchies for each level, enabling scalable address translation and independent optimization of rendering quality and memory.
